claims.text: A graph neural network can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The graph neural network will reduce mean absolute prediction error by at least 15% relative to current predictions.
The target materials are high-entropy alloys in the as-cast state.
The proposed intervention is training a graph neural network on high-entropy alloys with known phonon thermal conductivity values.
Temperatures from 300 K to 1000 K are relevant operating conditions for the proposed thermal-insulation application.
The complex multi-principal-element compositions of high-entropy alloys affect phonon scattering.
The complex multi-principal-element compositions of high-entropy alloys affect thermal conductivity.
A graph neural network can learn composition and structural patterns correlated with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Learning these composition and structural patterns enables accurate phonon thermal conductivity predictions.
The model will predict phonon thermal conductivity within 0.5 W/m-K of the true value.
Molecular dynamics simulations and empirical models represent the current prediction baseline.
The approach is applicable only to high-entropy alloys whose compositions and structures resemble those represented in the training dataset.
Training-data accuracy, graph neural network architecture, and transfer to unseen compositions are potential sources of uncertainty.
A blinded comparison against experimental measurements can benchmark the graph neural network against current prediction methods.
Time-domain thermoreflectance or laser flash analysis can provide the phonon thermal conductivity values used in the benchmark.
The hypothesis is falsified if the graph neural network's mean absolute error is not at least 15% lower than that of the baseline methods.
